chunks: [A part of the same sermon about hope and fear in Allāh :]

He claims according to his own thinking that he hopes from Allāh. By Allāh, the Great, he speaks a lie. The position is that his hope (in Allāh) does not appear through his action although the hope of every one who hopes is known through his action. Every hope is so, except the hope in Allāh, the Sublime, if it is impure; and every fear is established except the fear for Allāh if it is unreal.
ai.seo_question: How does one verify if their hope in God is genuine according to Shia teachings?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) critiques the superficial claim of hope by linking it to tangible action, establishing that true *rijā'* is verified through deeds while false hope is inherently flawed. This passage highlights the Shia theological principle that hope must be balanced with fear, where genuine fear of God is a cause for spiritual growth rather than a source of despair. It underscores the integration of inner conviction and outer practice as the hallmark of a believer's state.
